newsitem.title: USA: CBOT RICE FALLS LATE ON HEDGE SELLING.
newsitem.headline: CBOT RICE FALLS LATE ON HEDGE SELLING.

text.p: CBOT rice futures opened higher on Wednesday but fell in late dealings as hedge selling cropped up, traders said.
"The world price was up," a floor source said. "We started higher on that but then we just collapsed.
USDA on Tuesday put the world grain price for long grain whole kernels at 13.97 cents per lb, versus 13.59 cents a week earlier.
"It sold off pretty dramatically," another trade source said. "There was some pretty good hedging. Every time we rallied we'd find more offers above the market."
Traders said locals were early sellers but commercials led the market lower. Term Commodities was said to be a key seller of November and buyer of January.
Rice ended 14 to 10 cents per cwt lower with September down 11 at $9.66-1/2. Volume was estimated by CBOT at 500 lots, compared with Tuesday's actual volume of 799 lots.
